assignmentHtml.task: Research MrBeast YouTube channel comprehensively. Find: (1) Stable channel ID (@MrBeast) and canonical URL. (2) Operator: Jimmy Donaldson (MrBeast). Company structure if known (MrBeast LLC etc.). (3) Channel creation date and earliest still-public upload. (4) Operating location and displayed country (USA). (5) Languages (English, plus dubbed channels). (6) Primary content category (challenges/philanthropy). (7) Content supply model: original high-budget personality content. (8) Representative series. Provide direct source URLs.
assignmentHtml.context: MrBeast is #6 with ~139B lifetime views per Communitrics snapshot dated September 2, 2026. Need verifiable facts with source links.
assignmentHtml.expected_output: A structured dossier for MrBeast with all requested fields, each with source URLs.

answerHtml:
MrBeast Channel Dossier

  1. CHANNEL ID AND CANONICAL URL
  • Channel ID: UCX6OQ3DkcsbYNE6H8uQQuVA
  • Handle: @MrBeast
  • Canonical URLs: https://www.youtube.com/@MrBeast and https://www.youtube.com/channel/UCX6OQ3DkcsbYNE6H8uQQuVA
  • Source: Wikidata entry Q57618112 lists both the channel ID (P2397) and handle (P11245 = @MrBeast); YouTube search results confirm the channel page.
  1. OPERATOR AND COMPANY STRUCTURE
  • Operator: James Stephen 'Jimmy' Donaldson (born May 7, 1998, Wichita, Kansas; raised in Greenville, North Carolina)
  • Channel management entity: MrBeast LLC, described as 'a limited liability company consisting of editors, producers, cameramen, and more' (Fandom wiki)
  • Holding company: Beast Industries (formed 2023), privately held, with Donaldson owning 'more than half'; CEO Jeff Housenbold (since Sept 2024)
  • Subsidiaries/brands: Feastables (CPG chocolate/snacks), Beast Games (reality competition), Lunchly (children's lunch kits JV with KSI & Logan Paul), MrBeast Studios (production), Viewstats (B2B creator analytics SaaS), Step (teen fintech, acquired Feb 2026), Beast Philanthropy (non-profit arm)
  • Valuation: $5.2B round led by Alpha Wave Global; additional $200M from BitMine (Jan 2026)
  • Sources: Wikipedia, everything-pr.com, mrbeast.fandom.com, LinkedIn
  1. CHANNEL CREATION DATE AND EARLIEST STILL-PUBLIC UPLOAD
  • Channel created: February 19–20, 2012 (Wikidata states Feb 20, 2012; Fandom wiki states Feb 19, 2012; both agree on February 2012)
  • First video uploaded: February 2012 under username 'MrBeast6000', featuring Minecraft/Call of Duty gameplay, wealth estimations of other YouTubers, and commentary
  • Earliest still-public upload on current @MrBeast channel: November 19, 2015 — 'MrBeast6000's First Video (So Bad lol)' (video description: 'This is the first video I uploaded to this channel!'), with 14.3M views as of retrieval
  • Pre-2015 videos (e.g., 'Worst Intros' series, early gaming content) were deleted when the channel pivoted direction
  • Sources: Wikidata, Fandom wiki, YouTube video page, Wikipedia
  1. OPERATING LOCATION AND DISPLAYED COUNTRY
  • Operating location: Greenville, North Carolina, USA (132-acre campus)
  • Displayed country: United States
  • LinkedIn lists HQ as 'Greenville, NC 27834, US'; company size 501–1,000 employees; industry 'Media Production'; founded 2012
  • Sources: LinkedIn, businessinsider.com, everything-pr.com
  1. LANGUAGES
  • Primary language: English
  • Dubbing strategy: Originally launched separate international channels (July 2021 onward) for Spanish (MrBeast en Español), Russian (MrBeast На Русском), Portuguese/Brazilian (MrBeast Brasil), French (MrBeast en Français), Japanese (MrBeast Japan), Hindi (MrBeast हिन्दী), Arabic (مستر بيست بالعربي), and Chinese (Bilibili). Most standalone channels stopped uploading in Dec 2022 in favor of multi-language audio tracks on the main channel.
  • Current full-video dub languages include: Arabic, Bengali, Czech (upcoming), French, German, Hindi, Indonesian, Japanese, Korean, Portuguese, Russian, Spanish, Thai, Turkish, Vietnamese, Chinese
  • Shorts-only dubs in 20+ additional languages (Gujarati, Malay, Tamil, Urdu, etc.)
  • YouTube confirmed MrBeast dubbed his most popular videos in 11 languages via the multi-language audio feature
  • Sources: mrbeast.fandom.com International channels page, blog.youtube (YouTube official)
  1. PRIMARY CONTENT CATEGORY
  • Genres: Stunts, challenges, game show, philanthropy, vlog (per Wikipedia infobox)
  • Three core formats: (a) stunt challenges requiring difficult/risky tasks, (b) 'junklord' experiments using unusually large quantities of a single product, (c) giveaway competitions awarding substantial cash/prizes often through games
  • Charity campaigns: Team Trees ($20M+ raised), Team Seas, Team Water
  • Content designed to maximize CTR and retention per YouTube algorithm; bold keywords like 'challenge' and '24-hours' in titles
  • Sources: Wikipedia, mrbeast.fandom.com
  1. CONTENT SUPPLY MODEL
  • Original, high-budget, personality-driven content produced in-house by MrBeast Studios under Beast Industries
  • Flagship video budgets reached ~$1 million each by 2022, funded by brand sponsorships and AdSense, with revenue reinvested into larger productions (self-perpetuating cycle per The Verge)
  • Example: '$456,000 Squid Game in Real Life!' cost $3.5M to produce ($2M sets/production, $1.5M prizes)
  • Over 250 employees (writers, editors, producers) as of 2023; team expanded to ~750 across Beast Industries campus
  • Revenue diversification: YouTube channels remain central but Feastables now out-earns YouTube + Beast Games combined (~$225M revenue in 2024)
  • Sources: Wikipedia, everything-pr.com
  1. REPRESENTATIVE SERIES / VIDEOS
  • '$456,000 Squid Game in Real Life!' (Nov 24, 2021; 942M+ views; $3.5M budget)
  • 'Counting to 100,000' (Jan 9, 2017; breakthrough viral video; ~44-hour ordeal)
  • 'Last to Leave' endurance challenge series (e.g., 'Last to Leave Their Circle Wins $500,000')
  • '$1 vs $1,000,000' comparison/hotel room series
  • Team Trees / Team Seas / Team Water (philanthropic campaigns)
  • Beast Games (Amazon Prime Video reality competition, 2024–present)
  • Early format: 'How to Get Famous' series (YouTube advice/commentary)
  • Sources: Wikipedia, Wikipedia ($456,000 Squid Game article), various
